title: The 10 Best Cordless Pressure Washers
subtitle: Battery-powered pressure washers and portable power cleaners for cars, bikes, patios and cleanup away from an outlet, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A cordless pressure washer runs on a battery and can pull water from a bucket, a lake or a garden hose, so it works where a plug-in washer can't. We ranked 10 current best-sellers on rating, review volume and features: whether a battery and charger come in the box, whether it runs on a battery from a real tool lineup, a brushless motor, and a hose of 20 feet or more. The spread is wide. Most handheld units are car and patio cleaners, and the EGO HPW3204 is the only one here with the output of a full-size plug-in washer. Prices run from $49.99 for the AOODIL kit to $879 for the EGO kit.
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

buyers_guide.q: Can a cordless pressure washer replace a plug-in one?
buyers_guide.a: Only the big ones. Handheld battery units are power cleaners for cars, bikes, boats, windows and patio furniture. For concrete, decks and siding you want 2,000 PSI or more, which on battery means a cart unit like the EGO HPW3204 at $879. If you have an outlet, a corded washer does that work for much less.

buyers_guide.q: Can I trust the PSI on budget handheld washers?
buyers_guide.a: Treat it as a ceiling, not a rating. Pressure and flow together take power: 1,500 PSI at 3 GPM needs roughly 2 horsepower of pump output, and a 21V handheld motor makes a fraction of that. WORX and EGO publish numbers that hold up. For unbranded units, compare reviews and runtime instead of the headline PSI.

No. Most of these draw water through a hose dropped into a bucket, pool or lake, and the WORX Hydroshot also connects to a 2-liter bottle. A weighted intake filter, like the one MIMYTH includes, keeps sand and leaves out of the pump. The Sun Joe WA24C-LTE carries its own 5-gallon supply.

Buy the bare tool only if you already own that battery platform: the WORX WG620.9 for Power Share owners or the ZixDeNex body for Milwaukee M18 owners. Otherwise a kit is cheaper than buying a tool, battery and charger separately.

buyers_guide.q: How long does a battery last?
buyers_guide.a: Listings claim 20 to 60 minutes per charge depending on battery size and pressure setting. Two-battery kits like the KEEPEAK, SEESII and AOODIL let you swap and keep going, which matters if you wash more than one car.
